final.memo:
The events of this summer have clarified that we are in a regime where market mechanics and liquidity risk dominate fundamental stock picking. The July reversal, where our energy longs and financial shorts both moved sharply against us, taught us a painful lesson: apparent diversification is thin protection when factor co-movement and funding pressures force liquidation [D05, D06]. 

We are operating in the dark regarding our current counterparty haircuts and redemption pipelines [D01, D03]. In such a regime, the temptation to hold for a recovery at 'distressed prices' is a trap; we must instead prioritize our ability to exit and survive. We are reducing gross exposure immediately to ensure we are not forced sellers when the next wave of volatility hits, regardless of the intrinsic value of our positions [D04, D05].
